A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decayed-identity-shortcut research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original MAE and diffusion experiments, classification and segmentation results, generation FID scores, and supplementary reconstruction and supervised ResNet analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds KNN evaluation, architecture configurations, and shortcut-scheduler experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed linear shortcut decay, encoder-decoder skip connections, residual zero initialization, and placement within MAE and diffusion models remain unchanged. Cosine and learnable shortcut weights are introduced as ablation alternatives, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet-1K, ImageNet-100, CIFAR-100, COCO validation images, and a small supervised ImageNet subset. Classification, semantic segmentation, reconstruction, and conditional/unconditional generation coverage is retained; KNN and additional architectures change evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3a adds cosine-scheduled and learnable shortcut-weight comparators to the existing ablation comparison. The named representation-learning baselines in Table 1, scaling alternatives in Table 3b, and U-ViT diffusion baseline are retained.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 adds KNN classification with K=20. Table 2 extends the architecture settings to include 1024-dimensional features and 18- and 24-layer encoders. These extend the evaluation design; the previously documented training budgets, splits, linear-probing procedures, and diffusion settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially revises the supporting analyses: Table 2 separates width/depth effects and examines cumulative decay, while Tables 3a and 5 evaluate cosine versus learnable weighting and learned layer coefficients. It removes v3's t-SNE analysis, Pearson-correlation panel, and Appendix B.1 ImageNet-1K decay-sensitivity study. Reconstruction and supervised ResNet analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 explicitly estimates Pearson correlations between effective rank and accuracy across training epochs in Figure 5c; v4 removes this statistical analysis and its estimates. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 adds KNN results, including 63.9% for the proposed method versus 27.4% for MAE, and substantial new architecture/scheduler results: for example, 86.0% LP for the 1024-dimensional, 24-layer configuration and 79.5% for learnable weights. These are newly reported settings, not improvements over matching v3 runs. Existing Table 1 FT/LP and Table 4 diffusion scores remain unchanged. The ImageNet-1K sensitivity scores of 69.8% and 68.9% and Pearson estimates are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 4–5 change layer indexing from 0 through L−1 to 1 through L, correcting the inconsistent terminal identity in v3's decay formula to alpha_L=alpha_min. However, the reindexed Equation 4 retains x0, introducing an input-index mismatch. The underlying expansion and effective-rank definition otherwise remain the same; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add an explicit KNN-performance claim, while the contribution statement about features having distinct cluster structures is dropped. The central claims concerning residual connections, semantic abstraction, low-rank features, and diffusion generation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 explains decay selection through encoder depth and cumulative attenuation, and newly limits applicability to contrastive learning because its objectives may favor higher-rank features. Its scheduler interpretation contains an inconsistency: Section 4.2 says cosine performs worse at both settings, although Table 3a shows 82.9% versus 81.8% for linear decay at alpha_min=0.7.

D1.justification: v4 specifies K=20 for KNN and adds Appendix A.4's statement that learnable weights receive no regularization beyond standard weight decay. It omits v3's explicit alpha_min=0.7 setting for the COCO visualization. Existing optimizer, learning-rate schedule, training duration, batch size, hardware, and runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds RankMe (Garrido et al., 2023) to qualify the low-rank argument for contrastive learning and revises the positioning against earlier residual scaling in small convolutional networks. References to Dosovitskiy et al. (2021) and Karras et al. (2020, 2022) are removed; most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized revisions to the abstract, related work, experimental discussion, and captions. Ablations and embedding analysis exchange subsection order, an Impact Statements section is added, and appendix subsections are revised. Most introductory, methodological, diffusion, and concluding prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with extensive figure and table resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is redesigned using retained visualizations and appendix generation examples; the t-SNE figure and Pearson panel disappear. Table 1 replaces objective/augmentation columns with KNN and category headings, Tables 2–3 expand, and a new learned-weight table replaces the removed appendix sensitivity table.

improvement.justification: The KNN evaluation and architecture/scheduler controls modestly strengthen evidence for representation quality and design choices, while the contrastive-learning limitation clarifies applicability. These gains are tempered by removal of ImageNet-1K sensitivity and Pearson-correlation evidence, plus the new scheduler interpretation and equation-indexing inconsistencies. The revision improves validation without resolving a major deficiency in the original paper.
